newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MAGIC ACQUIRE SEIKALY IN FIVE-PLAYER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MAGIC ACQUIRE SEIKALY IN FIVE-PLAYER DEAL.

text.p: The Orlando Magic, trying to fill the big gap left by Shaquille O'Neal's departure, acquired centre Rony Seikaly in a five-player deal with the Golden State Warriors on Saturday.
Orlando also got forward/center Clifford Rozier and a future second-round draft pick from Golden State for forward Donald Royal and centres Felton Spencer and Jon Koncak.

In Seikaly, the Magic get the centre they were looking for after O'Neal departed as a $120 million-plus free agent for the Los Angeles Lakers over the summer, and after Koncak went down with a season-ending knee injury in September.

Seikaly, a 6-foot-11 (2.11 metres) native of Greece, held out of training camp and missed Golden State's 97-85 loss to the Clippers Friday night. He played his first six seasons in the league with the Miami Heat before being dealt to the Warriors exactly two years ago.
Seikaly averaged 12.1 points and 7.8 rebounds in 64 games last year before missing the final 15 contests with a thumb injury. He averaged 14.8 points and 9.8 rebounds over 539 career games.

"With so few options available, we're delighted to get a player of Rony's calibre to anchor us at the centre position," said Magic general manager John Gabriel. "He along with Clifford will give us added size and experience in the frontcourt."

Rozier began his third NBA season Friday by going scoreless in five minutes off the bench. The 6-foot-11 (2.11 metres) former first-round draft pick averaged 5.1 points and 5.3 rebounds over 125 contests his first two seasons.
Seikaly and Rozier will be with the team when Orlando travels to Tokyo to meet the New Jersey Nets this Thursday and Friday.

Orlando had hoped Spencer would be the answer at centre after he was acquired from the Utah Jazz for two players and a draft pick in August. He started Friday and had four points and six rebounds in 19 minutes in a 96-92 loss to the Washington Bullets.

The 7-foot (2.13 metres) Spencer was the sixth overall pick in 1990 by Minnesota and played his first three seasons with the Timberwolves. He was traded to Utah following the 1992-93 campaign. Spencer averaged 6.7 points and 6.6 rebounds over 397 games his first six seasons.

The 7-foot (2.13 metres) Koncak would have been Orlando's starting centre if not for his knee injury. He appeared in 67 games with the Magic last season, averaging 3.0 points and 4.1 rebounds. Koncak played his first 10 seasons in the league with the Atlanta Hawks.

Royal played the 1989-90 campaign with Minnesota and the 1991-92 season in San Antonio before finding his niche with Orlando in 1992-93. Over four seasons with the team, he averaged 7.8 points and 3.4 rebounds.

"Donald has played a significant role as a backup and starter for this team and will be missed," Gabriel added. "While we would have liked to retain Felton, without him involved we could not execute the deal."

To make room on their roster, the Warriors waived guard Anthony Harris from the injured list, placed forwards Lou Roe and Andrew DeClercq on the injured list and moved forward Marcus Mann from the injured list to the suspended list.
